title: Detection thresholds of static and low frequency electric fields in people with electrohypersensitivity (EHS) and influencing factors
summary: Due to the energy transition in Germany new power lines will be built to transmit electric energy over long distances. One group that is particularly affected by this are people who report to be electrohypersensitive (EHS). They are reporting symptoms caused by the exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF). The aim of the current research is to investigate whether people with EHS are better at detecting electric fields compared to healthy people. Furthermore, we are doing an extensive medical and psychological assessment to determine potential relevant factors that affect the electric field detection abilities.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria EHS group:
- You are generally healthy
- You are between 18 and 79 years old
- You give your written consent to participate
- You describe yourself as electrohypersensitive

Inclusion criteria control groups:
- You are generally healthy
- You are between 18 and 79 years old
- You give your written consent to participate
- You have participated in the study „Bestimmung der menschlichen Perzeptionsschwelle in statischen elektrischen Feldern der Hochspannungs-Gleichstrom-Übertragung (HGÜ)“ (EK 320/15)
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria all groups:
- People who are pregnant
- People who wear electronic implants and non-removable piercings
- Abnormalities of the skin 
- Severe scarring in the arm area
- Persons with neurological or mental illnesses that impair their perceptive abilities (e.g. neuropathy).
- People taking psychoactive medication
- Persons with schizophrenia or schizotypal and delusional disorders
- Persons with acute suicidal tendencies
- Persons with claustrophobia

Exclusion criteria control groups:
- People with self-reported electrohypersensitivity
